review.verdict: NOT ACCEPTABLE for an execution decision as authored (lens P1, supervisor only). No P0: the module does nothing on import, refuses without explicit group, window, reservation and admission records, has no deletion, lock or network code, and bounds children with a kernel Job Object (create suspended, assign before resume, kill on close, no breakaway). Ambiguous cleanup leaves the slot HELD. Two P1 defects remain. (1) The Vitest parser cannot see skipped or todo cases, and G2 to G5 have no case inventory, so a hidden hook failure could still be accepted as GREEN or EXACT_PREDECLARED_RED_ONLY. (2) Git is not pinned. It is found by name, with the working directory set to the snapshot the subjects can write to, and runs outside the Job Object while producing the source-identity evidence. There are 8 P2 and 10 P3 findings. Everything here is inspected source or untested behaviour. Nothing was run. The window expired on 2026-10-06. This review authorises nothing.

checklist.item: 1a Activation and import safety
checklist.evidence: Inspected source at 90f4ebd. Lines :712-718 run runGroup only when argv[1] resolves to this file; the top level only defines constants and the WINDOWS_HELPER string. Lines :59-69 refuse unless --group, --window, --reservation and --admission are given, and unknown or duplicate options are refused. Line :454 refuses anything but win32. The file name matches no default Vitest or node --test pattern. With no arguments, parseOptions throws before any write.

checklist.item: 1b Authorisation and reservation binding
checklist.evidence: Lines :466-481 require window.directSamuelApproval===true, a non-empty approvalText, the manifest digest and source commit and tree, the group listed, an unexpired window of at most 4 hours, and an EXCLUSIVE_ACTIVE reservation bound to the lease. All of these are fields in self-written JSON files; the code itself says 'a file is not itself approval'. The preparation export materializeOwnedSnapshot (:348-366) has no CLI route, so it can only be reached by importing the module. It skips the self-hash and several window checks (QS-10).

checklist.item: 2 Input binding (manifest, sources, Node, Git SHA and tree, CRLF)
checklist.evidence: The manifest's raw sha256 is bound to the window, reservation, admission and ownership records (:456-488). Self-hash at :459: recomputed blob bytes d85b5a04 equal manifest.supervisor.sha256. Node path and sha are checked at :461-462 and PowerShell at :546-548. HEAD and tree equality, plus a blob-hash recomputation of every tracked file, at :299-315. Gaps: git itself is not pinned (QS-02); untracked files, fixtures and node_modules are not rechecked (QS-06); the hashes depend on LF bytes, which are fragile under autocrlf=true (QS-19).

checklist.item: 3 Process control (spawn, environment, cwd, deadlines, tree kill, ceilings, ambiguity)
checklist.evidence: shell:false with argv arrays (:42, :550-551). CreateProcess uses an absolute application name and MSVCRT quoting (:260, :295-298, :538); there is no shell in the chain. The environment is an allowlist without proxies (:50-58, :528-531), and NODE_OPTIONS comes from each manifest command (Q-9). cwd is the snapshot (:538). Termination is per Job (:245, :281-283) with no PID kill, and active-process limits apply (:256, :196). Ambiguity leaves the slot HELD (:654, :685). Gaps: duplicate Path/PATH keys (QS-04), execution policy (QS-05), no memory cap (QS-07), handle inheritance (QS-15).

checklist.item: 4 Output handling (separate streams, cap, disk, digests)
checklist.evidence: stdout and stderr stream to separate CreateNew files (:246). The first 4 MiB is kept along with the observed byte counts (:246, :579-580), and receipts carry the sha256 of each retained stream. On overflow the run aborts rather than truncating (:246); the manifest records this deviation from the Q-11 truncation recommendation (QS-13). The process-event file and helper outputs are not hashed (QS-14).

checklist.item: 5 Admission (observation, refusal path, group consumption, ordering)
checklist.evidence: The supervisor never samples resources itself. It validates recorded observations: floors, 20 GiB of disk, the heavy-job predicate id, freshness within 30 s (:436-451), and a maximum-floor pre-window observation (:475-477). A group-level refusal writes a refusal attempt with groupConsumed:false (:510-517). A refusal before a later heavy command comes after the group marker (:623, :635-637) and so consumes the group (QS-03). Nothing gives one run exclusive use (QS-08). Ascending-floor order is manifest text only.

checklist.item: 6 Evidence (unique folder, no overwrite, receipt contents, atomicity, no network)
checklist.evidence: Unique run root per runId (:369-373, :482). Each command folder is created with mkdir recursive:false (:524), and writes use 'wx' (:38). Receipts carry argv, cwd, env keys, NODE_OPTIONS, source, the manifest sha, the helper sha, timestamps, deadline, exit, abort, PID tree counts and stream digests (:574-582, :286). The supervisor has no network API. Writes are not atomic, a few file digests are missing, and neither the window digest nor approvalText is recorded (QS-14, QS-10).

checklist.item: 7 Cleanup scope (owned only, no dist outside snapshot, traversal guards)
checklist.evidence: The supervisor has no rm, unlink or rmdir. Cleanup is TerminateJobObject on the owned job only (:283), and the manifest snapshot.cleanup preserves roots. build.mjs:6@f581b6b runs rm("dist") relative to cwd, which is the owned snapshot. Paths created are guarded by ensureOwned and within (:33-37, :370, :377, :392, :399-408, :491-494, :523). No Docker volumes, ports or pagefile are touched; G8, G9 and the database category are deferred.

checklist.item: 8 G0 self-test defined and bounded per doc 49 Q-4
checklist.evidence: Manifest G0 covers exit 0 and 1 with exact stream separation, deadline kill, stdout and stderr caps, a refusal path, a real child tree with a peak of at least 2 and cleanup proven, and a one-file Vitest baseline, all within a 60 s wall. It departs from Q-4: the floor is 1536 MiB, with no 512 MiB cap enforced, and ceilings are 3, 4 and 8 processes. The manifest discloses both as proposals. The refusal case is weak (QS-11), there is no node-tap case (QS-09), bootstrap interruption is not dispatched, and the timing is unproven (QS-20). NOT RUN.

checklist.item: 9 Predicted-red handling (exact names, never relabelled, unexpected stops)
checklist.evidence: compareCaseSets (:93-114) requires the failed set to equal the predeclared names exactly, and the selected and expected-pass sets where those are bound. runnerVerdict stays FAILED, with disposition EXACT_PREDECLARED_RED_ONLY (:111-113). The protection gate keeps FAILED (:152-154). An unexpected disposition stops later commands (:655-658). Names are compared without the file (QS-12).

checklist.item: 9b Skipped/todo detection for G2-G5
checklist.evidence: The Vitest regex (:125) has no ↓ or □, which are the skip and todo symbols Vitest 4.1.10 prints (utils.BS4fH3nR.js:18-19). G2-G5 contracts carry no selectedNames, no expectedPasses and no count, so a hidden case cannot be detected (QS-01).

checklist.item: 10 Unauthorised execution, host danger, secret leak, pass without evidence
checklist.evidence: No accidental activation, no shell, no secret-named variables (:531), no proxies, no deletion. Risks: unpinned git runs outside the job with a cwd the subjects can write to (QS-02); a false green is possible through invisible skips (QS-01); memory is uncapped (QS-07). No P0 found.

findings.claim: The vitest-verbose parser cannot see skipped or todo cases, and G2-G5 bind no case inventory. A run with hidden cases can therefore be accepted as GREEN or EXACT_PREDECLARED_RED_ONLY.
findings.evidence: Inspected :125@90f4ebd: the symbol class is [✓✔√×✖⨯-], and :127 maps only '-' to skipped. Pinned Vitest 4.1.10 (package.json sha caa41f04 equals the manifest pin) prints skipped as ↓ and todo as □ (dist/chunks/utils.BS4fH3nR.js:18-19; VerboseReporter.onTestCaseResult). So those rows never appear and the check at :103 never fires. G2-G5 bind only targetFiles and expectedFailures; :106 and :163 accept when the failed set equals the predicted set and exit is 1. Nested describe hooks exist at f581b6b (static-document 4, vite-document 2, root-composition 2, notifications 2). A failing hook can mark that suite's cases skipped, so they disappear while the file stays observed. manifest.focusedGreen.rule claims skips are detected.
findings.fix: At :125-127 map ↓ to skipped and □ and · to todo. Parse Vitest's final 'Tests' summary line and require the parsed totals to equal it, with skipped and todo at 0 or equal to a predeclared list. Bind an exact case count or a full expected-pass name list for each G2-G5 command in the manifest.

findings.claim: Git is not pinned. It is spawned by name with cwd set to the snapshot the subjects write to, runs outside the Job Object and every ceiling, and its output is the HEAD, tree and ls-tree identity evidence.
findings.evidence: Inspected :42: spawnSync('git', …, {cwd}) with no absolute path or hash. sourceState(run.cwd) runs at :631 and again at :662, after the subjects have run in that cwd. Preparation uses it at :379-381 and :403. Node (:461-462) and PowerShell (:546-548) are pinned by path and sha; manifest.toolchain has no git entry. Untested behaviour: libuv's Windows search_path looks in cwd before PATH, trying .com and then .exe. A git.com or git.exe written to the snapshot root would therefore run unconfined, and could forge the before/after identity. Untracked files are not refused (QS-06).
findings.fix: Add manifest.toolchain.git with an absolute executable path and its sha256. Verify it in loadRun and in preparation, spawn it by absolute path, and run it from a cwd outside the snapshot with -C <snapshot> --no-optional-locks.

findings.claim: Each later heavy command needs an admission observation no more than 30 s old, with no request or wait. A miss after the group marker consumes the group, which contradicts Q-3 and the manifest.
findings.evidence: :623 writes `${group}.attempt.json` before the loop. :635-637 re-read the admission file for every later heavy command and every G7 command, and :441-442 require an observedAt within 30 s of now. A miss throws into :660, the group is consumed, and :619 forbids a retry. The supervisor neither signals nor waits. Affected: G0 (vitest-baseline is the 8th command), G1 (3 commands), G4 (2) and G7 (6). manifest.admission.observations says there is no sampling loop, and bounds.attemptVsGroup says a refusal leaves the group unused. That holds only for the loadRun path (:510-517).
findings.fix: Before each later heavy command, write <group>-<command>.admission-request.json and wait, up to a bound set in the manifest, for an observation dated after that request. On a miss or a shortfall, write a refusal receipt with groupConsumed:false and stop. Alternatively, admit each group once and drop the per-command re-observation.

findings.claim: The child environment can contain both 'Path' and 'PATH'. Windows PowerShell 5.1 ConvertFrom-Json is likely to reject that, which would abort every command before any job exists.
findings.evidence: :54-55 keep each key's original case; Windows normally uses 'Path'. :529 reads osEnvironment().PATH, which is undefined when the key is 'Path', and adds a second key 'PATH' holding only the node directory plus ';'. spec.environment (:537-545) is written to launch-spec.json and parsed at :170 by the pinned Windows PowerShell. Untested and host-dependent: PS 5.1 refuses keys that differ only by case. The helper would then exit non-zero and native would be null. The receipt would show cleanupProven false, the group would be consumed and the reservation HELD with nothing started.
findings.fix: Normalise environment keys case-insensitively: uppercase map, refuse duplicates, and look PATH up case-insensitively in osEnvironment and executeOwned. Add a G0 assertion on the child's PATH.

findings.claim: The helper runs through -File with no execution-policy handling, and the host policy is NOT PROVEN.
findings.evidence: :550 spawns powershell.exe with -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -File <ps1> -SpecPath. Windows PowerShell applies execution policy to -File scripts; the Windows client default is Restricted. If the script is refused, every command ends ABORTED with cleanupProven false (HELD), and G0 is consumed. manifest.toolchain.windowsHelper does not record the policy.
findings.fix: Choose one: record the effective policy as a pre-window fact; pass a hash-checked body through -EncodedCommand; or declare a process-scoped -ExecutionPolicy Bypass in the manifest and the approval text. Never change the machine or user policy.

findings.claim: Untracked and ignored drift is not refused. Fixtures created during preparation are not re-verified when commands run. node_modules is pinned by only 6 files.
findings.evidence: :316 records `dirty` (git status porcelain) but never checks it, and the before/after states (:631, :662) are not compared. The generated G0 fixtures (:390-397) and the HTTP RED/GREEN files (:398-412) are hashed only during preparation. checkDependencyPins (:427-435) covers 6 files: vitest.mjs, vitest/package.json, the tsx loader and package.json, tsc, and typescript/package.json. An untracked .env, an extra Vitest config, or an edited fixture between groups would go undetected.
findings.fix: Require the porcelain output to equal an untracked-path allowlist in the manifest, and compare before with after. Re-hash the generated and historical files before each command. Record a node_modules inventory digest during preparation and recheck it for each group.

findings.claim: No Job memory limit is set, so doc 49 Q-4's 512 MiB G0 bound and the group floors are not enforced.
findings.evidence: :256 sets only flags 0x2000|0x8 (kill on close, active processes), and :195 sets 0x2008. jobMemory and processMemory are never set. The manifest's windowsHelper.memory says native and total job memory are NOT capped. G0's ramFloorMiB 1536 is an admission floor, not a cap. V8 old-space flags do not bound native memory, esbuild or tsc.
findings.fix: Set JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY (0x200) to a per-command ceiling bound in the manifest. Map job message 10 to the abort 'job-memory-cap' and add a G0 case for it.

findings.claim: Nothing makes a run exclusive, so two heavy groups can run at the same time under one runId.
findings.evidence: The source has no lock. The marker is per group (:618-624), and the attempt counts are read and then written (:497-500, :620-622). G2, G3, G4 and G5 each require only G0 and G1, so two supervisor processes could run them concurrently. The only exclusivity is the self-attested reservation.state and noCompetingHeavyJob.
findings.fix: Before writing the group marker, create receipts/active-group.lock with flag 'wx', holding the group, pid and start time. Refuse to start if it exists, and remove it only when the group receipt has cleanupProven true; otherwise leave it in place (HELD).

findings.claim: The node-tap parser is first exercised inside G1's single attempt; G0 has no TAP fixture.
findings.evidence: G0's commands use only the self-test, admission-refusal and vitest-verbose kinds. The node-tap regex (:121) accepts any indentation, so nested subtests or a per-file wrapper row would be parsed. A wrapper row 'ok N - <path>' would trip the refusal at :100-101 and consume G1 (:619). The shape of Node 20.19 TAP output is NOT PROVEN. Doc 49 Q-4 warned that an unproven counter would consume the one mandatory HTTP attempt.
findings.fix: Add a G0 node-tap fixture with one pass, one fail, one test filtered out by name pattern and one nested subtest, each with exact expected rows. Have parseCases match only top-level TAP lines.

findings.claim: Authority is a format check on self-written JSON. The preparation path checks less than loadRun, and receipts do not bind the approval record.
findings.evidence: :466-474 accept directSamuelApproval===true and a non-empty approvalText. Group receipts (:680-681) keep only approvedAt, expiresAt and groups: no window digest and no approvalText. materializeOwnedSnapshot (:348-366) can only be reached by import. It does not check its own sha against manifest.supervisor.sha256 (that happens only at :459). It skips approvedAt <= now, approvalText, the 4-hour bound, preWindowObservation and the reservation state.
findings.fix: Add a --prepare CLI mode that applies the full window checks and the self-hash. Record the sha256 of the window, reservation and admission files, plus approvalText, in every receipt. Require the window digest to appear in a Samuel-authored record.

findings.claim: The refusal self-test passes on any exception, and it does not exercise the refusal-receipt path.
findings.evidence: :641-648 set refused=true on any throw from assertAdmission. By the 6th G0 command the group observation is likely more than 30 s old, so the refusal is probably for staleness, not the floor. loadRun's refusal writer (:510-517, groupConsumed:false) is never exercised.
findings.fix: Assert the message is 'REFUSED: RAM or disk admission floor not met' using a fresh copy of the observation, and exercise the refusal-receipt writer inside the run root.

findings.claim: Expected failures and passes are compared by name only, not by file and name.
findings.evidence: :96 uses file::name for identity, but :104-109 compare bare names. With commands over several files (G2 has 6, G3 has 5), a name shared across files can attribute a failure to the wrong file. manifest.focusedGreen.predictedFailures already carry the file.
findings.fix: Compare `${file}::${name}` for vitest-verbose, using lists in the manifest that include the file.

findings.claim: The stream cap aborts a healthy but verbose run, which consumes the group.
findings.evidence: :246 calls Stop(job,'stream-cap') once more than 4 MiB has been observed. Doc 49 Q-11 recommended truncation, and manifest bounds.streamPolicy records 'Abort on cap'. The G3 verbose run over 5 files has unknown output size.
findings.fix: Decide this explicitly in the approval. Alternatively, truncate with byte counts and parse cases from a separate --reporter=json --outputFile.

findings.claim: Receipt digests are incomplete, writes are not atomic, and the preparation-complete check is existence only.
findings.evidence: :574-582 leave out the sha256 of job-process-events.jsonl, launch-spec.json, the executed .ps1 bytes (only the in-memory string is hashed) and the helper raw outputs. :38 writes with 'wx' and no temp-file rename, so a crash leaves truncated JSON. :489 checks only that preparation-complete.json exists; it does not check its fields or that preparation-aborted.json is absent.
findings.fix: Hash each of these files into the receipt, write to a temp file and then link or rename, and validate the fields of preparation-complete.

findings.claim: The subject inherits every inheritable handle the helper holds, and the supervisor waits on 'close'.
findings.evidence: :260 calls CreateProcess with bInheritHandles=true, so the subject also gets the helper's own stdout and stderr pipes to Node and could write into the receipt stream. :563-566 wait on 'close', which needs every holder to exit. Kill-on-close normally ends them.
findings.fix: Use PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST with only the two child pipe ends, and resolve on 'exit' with a bounded wait for the streams to drain.

findings.claim: The Job does not set die-on-unhandled-exception.
findings.evidence: :256 sets flags 0x2000|0x8 only. A crashing child may wait on Windows Error Reporting until the deadline.
findings.fix: Add 0x400 (JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_DIE_ON_UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION) and set SetErrorMode in the helper.

findings.claim: In G7 a verdict-only command runs before the build, so its failure blocks artifact production, against the Q-1 split.
findings.evidence: The manifest G7 order runs no-em-dash-source first and build second. Supervisor :657 stops on any unexpected disposition, so a verdict-only failure prevents build and no-em-dash-build.
findings.fix: Order build and no-em-dash-build first, followed by the verdict commands.

findings.claim: The documentation and authoring are imprecise in several places.
findings.evidence: The header at :6 says --manifest is required, but :66 does not require it (it defaults at :22). selfTestDefinitions (:694-710) is unused and differs from the manifest's G0 (stream-cap versus stdout-cap; expectOwnedChildren versus minimumPeakJobChildren). preWindowObservation has no observedAt (:475-477). g0Acceptance is not bound to the G0.group.json digest (:606-611).
findings.fix: Require --manifest, derive the G0 definitions from the manifest or drop the export, add observedAt, and add g0Acceptance.g0GroupSha256.

findings.claim: The raw self-hash and manifest hash depend on LF bytes in a checkout where core.autocrlf is true.
findings.evidence: :459 and :456-458 hash raw working-tree bytes. The builder has core.autocrlf=true. The .gitattributes at 90f4ebd covers only evidence/*.log and the patches; git check-attr reports text unspecified for both files. Working-tree bytes equal the blobs today, but a fresh checkout would write CRLF and every refusal check would fire (fail-closed).
findings.fix: Add 'qualification-supervisor.mjs -text' and 'evidence/*.json -text'.

findings.claim: The G0 timing and process bounds are not proven against compiler cold start or the full-repository inventories.
findings.evidence: :562 gives trivial commands a 5 s outer limit covering PowerShell start, Reflection.Emit, compilation by Add-Type and the subject. With maxOwnedProcesses 3 the bootstrap limit is 2 (:541, :196), which must cover PowerShell plus csc and any other process the job counts. The two sourceState passes, over 6,069 files and 211,933,351 bytes, fall inside the 60 s. manifest.g0.unmetAcceptance lists the cold-start process cap as NOT_RUN.
findings.fix: Move the source inventory out of the group wall into an attested preparation step. Separate compilation from the command wall, or approve higher G0 bounds explicitly.

Inspected: :125@90f4ebd uses the class [✓✔√×✖⨯-], which cannot match Vitest 4.1.10's skip and todo symbols (vitest/dist/chunks/utils.BS4fH3nR.js:7,:14,:19-20; the lens cited :18-19, off by one). [P2, plausible, host-dependent] The Windows env key case breaks the helper. osEnvironment:50-58 keeps the original key case ('Path' on most Windows launches), but executeOwned:529 reads osEnvironment().PATH case-sensitively. That yields PATH=<node dir>; (no system path) alongside the full 'Path'. JSON.stringify then writes both keys to launch-spec.json, and Windows PowerShell ConvertFrom-Json (:170) refuses case-variant duplicate keys, with $ErrorActionPreference Stop. The helper then emits no receipt, so every command aborts and G0 is consumed. Node's own spawn keeps the lexicographically first, 'PATH' (node dir only), so git-calling children (the protection gate :180, route-uniqueness, migration-dag) may not find git. Fix: normalise allowlisted keys to upper case and drop case variants before merging.
